# DG Roam Load Extension

Use this skill for one complete lifecycle: build `apps/roam`, open an authenticated slot, register `apps/roam/dist`, activate it, verify DG runtime readiness, run an optional caller test, capture proof, and close.

It composes with `dg-roam-playwright-session` for account/profile selection.

## Quick Start

```sh
pnpm --filter roam playwright:load-extension -- --slot 1
```

Use another slot for isolated work:

```sh
pnpm --filter roam playwright:load-extension -- --slot 2
```

The script builds by default, verifies `window.roamjs.extension.queryBuilder`, checks the DG settings UI, and writes proof under `local/roam-playwright/artifacts`.

To add feature-specific assertions without copying the loader, pass an ESM test module:

```sh
pnpm --filter roam playwright:load-extension -- --slot 1 --test-module ./local/roam-playwright/feature-proof.mjs
```

```js
export default {
  readySelector: "[data-testid='feature-ready']",
  async ready({ page }) {
    return page.evaluate(() => Boolean(window.myFeature?.ready));
  },
  async run({ page, outDir }) {
    await page.getByText("Expected output").waitFor();
    return { assertion: "passed" };
  },
  async cleanup({ page, state }) {
    // Remove only fixtures created by run().
  },
};
```

`run()` starts only after the standard DG runtime proof and any caller readiness hook succeeds. `cleanup()` runs when `run()` started, including after a failed assertion. Return JSON-serializable proof values.

## Options

- `--slot 1|2|3`: Select the Roam account/profile.
- `--skip-build`: Load the existing `apps/roam/dist` without rebuilding.
- `--headed`: Run with a visible Chromium window.
- `--keep-open`: Leave the browser open after loading.
- `--dist <path>`: Load a different Roam extension folder. Use only when intentionally testing another build output.
- `--registration-name <name>`: Developer Extensions row name. Defaults to the built folder name, usually `dist`.
- `--test-module <path>`: Caller readiness, test, and cleanup hooks. Absolute Windows paths and paths containing spaces are supported.
- `--out <path>` and `--screenshot-name <name>`: Proof artifact locations.
- `--timeout <ms>`: UI and readiness timeout. Defaults to `45000`.

## Folder Loading

Roam Depot's folder button calls `window.showDirectoryPicker()`, not an `<input type="file">`. The script installs a temporary in-page directory-picker shim backed by the files in `apps/roam/dist`.

The loader uses native Playwright clicks for developer mode and folder controls. It treats the extension row as registration only, then clicks the header or row refresh control when present and waits for DG runtime proof. Roam versions that activate automatically may expose no refresh control.

An IndexedDB clone warning for the fake directory handle is expected and classified separately. Other page exceptions fail the run. `last-run.json` includes phase timings and bounded browser diagnostics; failures also capture a dedicated screenshot and compact DOM state.

## Safety Notes

- Do not commit `.env`, browser profiles, or artifacts.
- Do not commit real Roam test account emails, graph names, graph URLs, or proof screenshots.
- Keep feature fixtures, command interactions, and assertions in the caller module. Do not add them to the generic loader.
- Do not change Supabase local/branch/production config as part of this skill.
- Do not run production-backend smoke tests in this workflow.

input.content:
---
name: reference_roam_loader_canvas_driving
description: Driving the Roam tldraw canvas from playwright:load-extension needs a dev build, the settings dialog closed, and the camera centred per shape
metadata:
  type: reference
---

Three things block `pnpm --filter roam playwright:load-extension --test-module` from driving the Roam tldraw canvas. All three fail *silently* as clean false negatives, not errors.

1. **`window.tldrawApps[pageTitle]` is the editor handle, but only in a dev build.** `apps/roam/scripts/build.ts` defaults `NODE_ENV` to `production`, which compiles the registration out entirely (`grep -c tldrawApps dist/extension.js` → 0). Build with `NODE_ENV=development npx tsx scripts/build.ts`, run the loader with `--skip-build`, then rebuild production afterwards so the worktree's `dist` is not left a dev artifact.
2. **The loader leaves the Roam settings dialog open** after its DG proof step. Every canvas click lands on the modal overlay instead. Press Escape until `.bp3-dialog, .bp3-overlay-open` is gone, in `ready()` *and* after the canvas mounts.
3. **Centre the camera per shape before clicking.** `zoomToFit()` across a row of fixtures puts the outer ones off-canvas or under the style panel; `editor.setCamera({x: -midX + 400, y: -midY + 300, z: 1})` makes every click land.

Always make the probe prove the menu opened before judging its contents — assert tldraw's own entries (`Duplicate|Delete|Copy as|Export as|Select all`) are present, else "menu did not open" scores as "menu without the item you're testing". A locked shape gets a reduced menu (no Duplicate/Delete), so include `Export as|Select all` in that marker.

Canvas pages are pages whose title matches `DEFAULT_CANVAS_PAGE_FORMAT` (`Canvas/*`), so a test module can make one with `roamAlphaAPI.data.page.create` and open it.

Related: [[reference_pr_evidence_worktree_roam_profile]], [[reference_pr_evidence_roam_login]], [[reference_tldraw_store_put_no_listener]], [[reference_roam_ext_dev_symlink_contested]]

content.text:
All four tasks done. Taking your two questions first, since the answers changed what I built.

## `getConvertibleShapeText` — fixed

The helper returned `null` / `""` / `"text"`, where **`""` meant "convertible" but is falsy**. Only images hit that branch. Any future caller writing the natural `if (shapeText)` would have silently dropped images from the Convert To menu and the `?C` dialog — no type error, the menu item just vanishes.

It's now two functions with no ambiguous value:

```ts
export const getShapeText = (shape: TLShape): string =>
  "text" in shape.props ? shape.props.text : "";

export const isConvertibleShape = (shape?: TLShape | null): boolean => { … }
```

The gate is a plain boolean, and the prefill is fetched only on the path that needs it — which also removed the oddity where the image path computed `shapeText` and threw it away.

**I did not touch `ImageConvertOverlay`.** Its `isConvertibleImage` is a TypeScript type guard (`shape is TLImageShape`) that the overlay depends on for narrowing; sharing would mean repeating the type check anyway. Still a drift risk, still your call.

## Live verification — 9 of 9, on a real graph

The credentials appeared in the main repo's `apps/roam/.env` since I last looked, so I pointed the worktree at them and at the signed-in `playwright-1` profile.

| Fixture | Convert To | |
|---|---|---|
| text shape (with text) | offered | regression check |
| text shape (empty) | offered | unchanged behavior |
| **rectangle with text** | **offered** | new |
| **sticky note with text** | **offered** | new |
| empty rectangle | absent | as designed |
| whitespace-only rectangle | absent | trim works |
| empty sticky note | absent | as designed |
| arrow with label | absent | still Relation only |
| locked rectangle | absent | |

**My first run reported a clean sweep of false negatives** — every fixture, including the pre-existing text case, came back "no Convert To". The loader leaves the Roam settings dialog open over the canvas, so every right-click hit a modal. I'd have reported a working feature as broken. The probe now asserts tldraw's own menu entries are present before judging, so "menu didn't open" can't be scored as "menu without Convert To"; that's what caught the locked case being inconclusive rather than passing.

I built with `NODE_ENV=development` to get the `window.tldrawApps` hook (production compiles it out), then **rebuilt production** so the worktree's `dist` isn't left a dev artifact. Nothing from the run is tracked — the proof modules live in gitignored `local/`.

## State

**CI: 9 passing, 0 failing, `MERGEABLE`/`CLEAN`.** The rebase needed no conflict resolution — GitHub's `CONFLICTING` was stale duplicate commits from a base force-push, including one the base had since reverted; `rebase --onto` dropped them. Both Codex threads fixed, replied to, resolved. PR body updated with the fixture table.

Two things still open: `reviewDecision` is `CHANGES_REQUESTED` from the original Codex pass and needs a re-review to clear, and **the automated run covers which shapes offer the option, not where the node lands**. The frame and group placement cases — the ones the delegated review caught me half-fixing — still want a hand-driven Loom before merge.

content.text:
I can't record a Loom — that needs your account and their app — so I produced an mp4 instead: **41s, 10fps, captions burned in, visible cursor, paced for human reading.** It's above.

## What it shows

**Scene 1 — rectangle inside a frame.** Right-click → Convert To → Claim → Confirm. The green discourse node ends up inside the frame at the same spot.

| | parent | local x/y | page x/y |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | `shape:demo_frame` | 80,90 | 380,290 |
| after | `shape:demo_frame` | 80,90 | 380,290 |

Without `parentId`, tldraw would have read `80,90` as *page* coordinates and dropped the node near the canvas origin.

**Scene 2 — one of two grouped shapes.** The group dissolves exactly as `GroupShapeUtil.onChildrenChange` specifies, the node's parent becomes `page:page`, and the page point stays `320,240`. This is the case `parentId` alone did **not** cover: the child's group-relative x/y were `0,0`, so without the page-point fallback the node would have landed at page `0,0`. That's the half-fix the delegated review caught, now proven fixed.

## Two things the recording turned up

Both are real behavior worth knowing, and I've added them to the PR:

- **Clicking a grouped shape selects the group**, and Convert To is correctly not offered for a group — you have to enter the group first.
- **Double-clicking to enter a group also starts editing the shape's label**, so the first right-click after it just dismisses the editor rather than opening the menu. Cost me two runs before I stopped guessing and instrumented the selection state.

## State

PR body updated with the measured before/after numbers. Production `dist` restored (I'd built with `NODE_ENV=development` for the `window.tldrawApps` hook). The demo created two real Claim pages in the dev graph; cleanup deleted them along with the canvas pages.

---
name: pr-evidence
description: Upload verification screenshots to the Roam dev graph and get public image URLs plus a Markdown table for the PR body. Use after a verification run produced PNGs and before create-pr writes the Evidence section.
---

# PR evidence upload

Uploads PNGs through `roamAlphaAPI.file.upload` in an authenticated Roam Playwright slot, files them under a page in the slot's graph (`discourse-dev-graph`), and emits a Markdown table that create-pr pastes into the Evidence section.

## When to use

- After verification (Roam `load-extension` run, Obsidian CDP run, manual captures) left PNGs on disk.
- Before create-pr builds the body. Roam PRs: reuse the verification's slot once that run has closed. Obsidian PRs: omit `--slot`.

## Command

Run from the worktree root, using the worktree's own `tsx` so the relative PNG paths and the repo's Playwright resolve:

```sh
./apps/roam/node_modules/.bin/tsx ~/.claude/skills/pr-evidence/upload.ts \
  [--slot N] [--branch <b>] [--label "<YYYY-MM-DD · shortsha · harness>"] [--harness <name>] \
  [--out table.md] [--settle-ms 5000] \
  shot1.png="Empty state" shot2.png="After import" ...
```

- `pnpm --filter roam exec tsx ...` also works, but it changes cwd to `apps/roam`, so pass absolute PNG paths.
- `--branch` defaults to the current git branch. `--label` defaults to `<today> · <short sha> · <--harness or "manual">`.
- Caption defaults to the file name without extension.
- No `--slot`: tries each configured slot (1, 2, 3) and moves on only on a profile-lock error.
- Headless by default (`HEADLESS=false` to watch).

## Output contract

- stdout: JSON `{page, pageUid, branchBlockUid, runBlockUid, items: [{caption, url, blockUid}]}`.
- stderr: `Markdown table: <path>`. The file defaults to `pr-evidence-<runBlockUid>.md` next to the first PNG and contains `| Scenario | Screenshot |` rows with `![caption](url)`. create-pr pastes it as-is.
- URLs are public Firebase storage links (`200 image/png` without cookies, verified 2026-09-23).

## Roam structure

```
Trang test/                       (page, found or created)
  <branch>                        (top-level block, reused on every run)
    <date · sha · harness>        (new run block per invocation, appended last)
      <caption> ![](<url>)        (one per PNG)
```

## Gotchas

- Imports `apps/roam/scripts/playwright/roamSession.ts` from the current worktree (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`), so profiles live in that worktree's `local/roam-playwright/profiles/` unless `DG_ROAM_PLAYWRIGHT_PROFILE_DIR_<n>` is set.
- A slot's profile can only be open once. Close the verification session first, never delete lock files.
- Login errors (expired session, 2FA) come from `openRoamSession`; recover with `pnpm --filter roam playwright:open -- --slot N --headed --allow-login`, then rerun.
- Never print values from `apps/roam/.env`.
- Uploads cannot be rolled back and Roam cannot list graph files, so don't loop retries on a failing run.
- tsx injects `__name()` into functions passed to `page.evaluate`; the script shims it in the page first. Keep that shim if you edit the in-page code.

**No — there's no Loom MCP**, and it wouldn't help if there were. I checked both:

- The MCP registry returns nothing for loom/video/screen-recording (only PubMed and Figma, both irrelevant).
- **Loom has no public upload API.** Uploading is a manual web-UI action (`New Video → Upload Video`), and it's gated to Business/Business+/Enterprise plans. There are third-party Loom *downloader* APIs on Apify, but nothing for upload.

So no tool can put this in Loom for you. Three things that actually work, in order of how good the result is:

**1. Drag the mp4 into the PR comment box** — 349 KB, ~10 seconds of your time. GitHub uploads it to its own CDN and renders a real inline player with scrubbing. This is the only route to an embedded video on GitHub; the upload endpoint isn't in the public REST API, so `gh` can't do it.

**2. Let me embed it as a GIF, fully automated.** I already made one to check feasibility: **780 KB** at 900px wide, 8fps — small enough that `pr-evidence` can upload it to the dev graph and I can drop `![](url)` straight into the PR body, where GitHub renders it inline. No manual step. Trade-off: no scrubbing, no pause, and the captions are slightly softer at 900px. That's the realistic substitute for a Loom embed.

**3. Upload the mp4 itself via pr-evidence** — works and gives a public Firebase URL, but GitHub renders it as a plain link, not a player. Strictly worse than either of the above.

Worth saying plainly: the PR body already carries the *evidence* — measured parent ids and page coordinates before and after, for both the frame and the group case. The video is for reviewer confidence, not proof, so option 1 whenever you next have the PR open is probably the right call and costs me nothing.

Uploaded, but **it does not get you an inline video**, and the reason is worth knowing because it affects more than this PR.

## What happened

Both files are up and publicly reachable (HTTP 200):
- **mp4** (349 KB) — now linked in the PR body as a download
- **gif** (780 KB) — uploaded, but unusable for embedding, see below

## The blocker

Roam's `file.upload` serves **everything** as `content-type: application/octet-stream`. GitHub proxies external images through `camo.githubusercontent.com`, which requires `image/*` and returns **400** otherwise. I tested it rather than assuming: rendered the markdown via `gh api /markdown`, pulled the camo URL it generated, and fetched it.

```
GIF via camo → HTTP 400
PNG via camo → HTTP 400
```

**That second line is the important one.** It's not about video. A plain pr-evidence screenshot fails the same way, so **every `![](firebase…)` image in your recent PRs is almost certainly rendering broken on GitHub right now.** The skill's own contract still claims `200 image/png without cookies, verified 2026-09-23` — that's gone stale since.

I tried patching `upload.ts` to infer MIME from the extension. It made no difference: the file already went up as `image/png` and still came back octet-stream, so Roam or its storage layer overrides the client-side type. Dead code, so **I reverted it** — your skill file is byte-for-byte as it was.

## Where that leaves the video

There is no automated route to an inline video on this PR. Loom has no upload API, no Loom MCP exists, and GitHub's attachment upload is browser-only. The mp4 link in the body will download a 349 KB file a reviewer can play locally — that's the honest ceiling without you touching it. **Dragging the mp4 into the PR comment box is still the only way to get a real player**, and it stays ~10 seconds of work.

The PR's actual evidence — measured parent ids and page coordinates before and after, for both the frame and the group case — is unaffected and already in the body.

# Scope Check

Compare the completed change with its acceptance boundary. Return a copy-ready `Scope check` section unless the user requests the analysis too.

## Gather the Inputs

1. Resolve the Linear issue from an explicit `ENG-###` identifier, then from the PR or branch name. Fetch the issue with the Linear connector. If it is unavailable, ask for the ticket's `Problem`, `Solution`, and `Done When` sections.
2. Treat `Done When` as the acceptance boundary. Use `Problem` and `Solution` only to clarify that boundary, not to silently expand it.
3. Resolve the final change set from the supplied diff or PR. For a PR, inspect its metadata and complete diff. For the current branch, compare it with the PR base branch and include staged and unstaged changes.
4. Read linked decisions or ticket comments only when they explain an apparent scope expansion.

## Evaluate Scope

Map every material behavior or architectural change to a `Done When` criterion.

- Treat implementation details, tests, documentation, and generated files required to satisfy `Done When` as in scope.
- Flag broader abstractions, unrelated refactors, new dependencies, migrations, or support for cases not required by `Done When`.
- Do not treat a change as in scope only because it is useful or adjacent.

For each scope expansion, determine:

1. What broader abstraction or additional case was introduced?
2. Which current use case or ticket requires it, and why must it be included now rather than deferred?
3. Was anyone affected or consulted, and where is the discussion or decision recorded?

Do not invent missing justification. Mark it `Not documented` and recommend recording it in a Linear comment before the PR is merged.

## Format the Result

Use this form when the diff stays within scope:

```markdown
## Scope check

- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-#### and the final diff.
- Scope beyond `Done When`: None.
```

Use this form when the diff expands scope:

```markdown
## Scope check

- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-#### and the final diff.
- Scope beyond `Done When`: <what changed>
- Required now: <use case or ticket and why it cannot be deferred>
- Anyone affected or consulted: <Yes, No, or Not documented>
- Decision: <link to the discussion or decision, or `Not documented`>
```

If the ticket or diff cannot be resolved, leave the checkbox unchecked and state exactly what input is missing. Keep findings short and evidence-based.

Do not modify the issue, PR, or implementation unless the user explicitly asks.

=== PR_GUIDELINES.md ===
# PR guidelines

This is the repository source for the DevOps PR process. Code standards live in [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md); agent instructions live in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). Production changes, releases, and work intake remain in DevOps.

## Scope and structure

- Use one PR per Linear ticket. You may batch very minor, unrelated changes of a few lines when they are low risk.
- Scope the ticket to one specific problem. If additional problems need attention, pause that additional work and check with the team or lead before implementing it.
- Use separate PRs for unrelated refactors, feature additions, dependency updates, and lint or style fixes. Keep scope to a single package or app when possible.
- For features spanning packages, make foundational changes such as types and shared utilities first, then use separate PRs for usage and integration.

## Size and review guidance

About 200 added plus removed lines is a useful target. Up to 400 lines is acceptable when the change is scoped and self-contained. Ideally, touch fewer than five files; repetitive mechanical changes can justify more. These are review guidelines, not automatic rejection thresholds.

Test changes do not count toward the 400-line threshold.

Above 400 changed lines, explain why the PR cannot reasonably be split. Include the main review entry points and intended testing path in Reviewer brief. Keep this concise rather than adding a file-by-file summary.

## Branches and PR metadata

- Use Linear's generated branch name through Copy Branch Name.
- For Linear-backed work, use `ENG-#### Exact Linear ticket title` as the PR title. This is the repository convention in place of the alternative title formats previously listed in DevOps.
- Start with [.github/pull_request_template.md](.github/pull_request_template.md). Treat the ticket as the source of truth rather than restating it. Follow the PR body guidance in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#pull-request-bodies).

## Before requesting review

- Run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, then `pnpm ci:validate` from the repository root before opening a PR or declaring it ready. Resolve failures before requesting review. A draft must disclose unresolved validation blockers.
- Check applicable build and lint commands. Manually exercise changed behavior end-to-end, including relevant edge cases and alternative flows. Verification is optional; use it when checks and results help the reviewer.
- Read the complete final diff and review it against [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md), including added and modified comments. Use inline PR comments for review-specific explanations and durable code comments for constraints future changes must preserve.
- Run `$scope-check` against the ENG ticket and final diff. Paste its Scope check section into the PR body. If `Done When` is missing, leave the checkbox unchecked and state that explicitly.
- Run `$dg-pr-adherence-check` against the final diff and PR metadata. Check the Standards check box when it has run. Make any outstanding findings or unverified requirements known to the PR author so they can address them.
- Complete the Local delegated full review required by the template, using `$dg-delegated-full-review` when no other full-review workflow is available.
- Include a Loom video for every PR, including backend, refactor, and infrastructure changes. Keep it under 2–3 minutes, show before/after for bug fixes, and narrate key decisions. Put the link in Loom video.
- Assign a reviewer when ready. Do not mark a draft ready while required evidence or reviews remain incomplete.

## After merge

Delete the PR branch after a successful merge. Creating a draft does not authorize merging or deleting branches.

## Merge-ready

**`MERGEABLE` / `CLEAN` · `APPROVED` · 9 checks passing, 0 failing · 0 unresolved threads.**

### Conflict

Not a text conflict. **#1427 squash-merged into main**, GitHub auto-retargeted this PR's base to `main`, and my branch still carried the unsquashed eng-1356 commits — hence 7 files and a dirty state. I replayed only the ENG-1884 commits onto main.

Compatible intents, so the merged version keeps both. Side effect: `parentId` is now main's, so my scope expansion shrank.

### CI

`validate` showed as failed — it was **cancelled** at 15m02s with no failed steps, not a real failure. It has passed in ~1m25s on every run since.

### Comments

Zero unresolved threads. Both Codex threads from the earlier head remain fixed and resolved.

### Three things I got wrong and caught

- `git add -A` swept **278 demo PNGs** into the merge commit — `.gitignore` has `local/*`, which is root-anchored, so `apps/roam/local/` isn't covered. Untracked and amended out before it landed.
- `ci:validate` reported `FULL TURBO`, 6/6 cached, right after rebasing onto a different base. Re-ran with `TURBO_FORCE=true`: 6/6, **0 cached**, 630 tests.
- A receipts hook blocked me from ticking review boxes against a stale head, three separate times. Each was correct — I re-ran all three checks per head.

### Where I stopped

Three review rounds, each finding no blocking defects but each surfacing a new Low in the code from the round before. I took two (`pagePoint` read live against a stale snapshot; then that read still sitting behind the `await`) and **stopped** rather than keep patching. Two remain open and documented in the body:

1. **The re-read doesn't re-check `isLocked`.** `deleteShapes` silently skips locked shapes, so one locked during the sizing query would survive with a duplicate node on top. One-line guard, but whether it returns silently or toasts is a product call — the Roam page is already created by then.
2. **The dialog's error message** says "a sticky note or shape containing text", which also describes a labelled arrow, and arrows are deliberately excluded.

Both are narrow and non-blocking. Say the word and I'll take either.

### Bots

Two items still unresolved from before: **no unit tests** for `isConvertibleShape`/`getShapeText`, and my open question on adding an unanchored `local/` to `.gitignore` — the thing that would have prevented the 278-file mistake.
